title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is working out the structure of an algebraic group scheme attached to a pair (ρ,σ) of 2×2 matrices. The motivating example on the next page is the 'modular case' ρ=[[0,1],[-1,1]] (order 6) and σ=[[0,-1],[1,0]] (order 4), which generate SL2(Z). The group is SG*_{ρ,σ}. By the previous page it is a semidirect product SG*_{ρ,σ}(0)·Λ_0, so he reduces to the factor SG**_{ρ,σ}(0). That factor sits inside T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ and is cut out by equations (20). Here T_ρ is the centraliser torus of ρ, N'_σ is a normaliser-type group of σ containing the torus T_σ with index 2, and T_0 is a one-dimensional torus.

This page:
1. The map T_0 → G_m, u ↦ det u, is an isomorphism.
2. Hence in the triple (u,a,b) the component u is determined by (a,b) through equations (20). The data can be written in coordinates (α,β,μ,ε) = (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, det u, ε(b)).
3. So the projection SG**(0) → T_ρ × N'_σ, (u,a,b) ↦ (a,b), is a monomorphism. Its image is the subgroup defined by det b = ε' det a with ε'^2 = 1, i.e. (det b)^2 = (det a)^2.
4. Equivalently, writing δ_ρ: T_ρ → G_m and δ_σ: N'_σ → G_m for the determinant characters, the image is the inverse image of the diagonal of G_m × G_m under (δ_ρ^2, δ_σ^2).
5. Since δ_ρ and δ_σ are epimorphisms, the homomorphism (u,a,b) ↦ (ε(b), det b / det a) to μ2 × μ2 is an epimorphism.
6. The next page draws the consequences. There is an exact sequence 1 → SG°(0) → SG*(0) → μ2×μ2 → 1. The kernel SG° is {(a,b) ∈ T_ρ × T_σ : det a = det b}. It is in turn an extension of G_m by ST_ρ × ST_σ, the kernels of the determinant characters.

This is a routine dévissage, into tori and finite pieces, of a group scheme of symmetries attached to a representation of the modular group. It belongs to Grothendieck's study of the 'équation des lacets' in rank 2.
errors: The sign ε(b) records the component of N'_σ (whether b lies in T_σ or in the other coset). It is a priori a map to the constant group Z/2, not to μ2; the two differ in characteristic 2, which is precisely a case Grothendieck singles out on the next page. Writing μ2×μ2 for the target is therefore slightly imprecise there.

Two numbering clashes: equation labels (21) and (22) here are reused from the previous page, and the target of the projection is written T_ρ × N'_σ although the previous page says the subgroup lies in T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ. These are bookkeeping slips, not mathematical errors.

The surjectivity onto μ2×μ2 is fine if 'épi' is read fppf-locally, using surjectivity of δ_ρ and of ε on N'_σ. The fraction under ε' (det b/det a over det(u a^{-1})) is somewhat garbled, but given the relation between u and a it is consistent with ε' = ±1.

ideas.what: Elimination of the T_0 component via the isomorphism det: T_0 ≅ G_m, making the projection to T_ρ × N'_σ a monomorphism
ideas.modern_name: Description of a subgroup scheme as a graph / fibre product

ideas.what: Image described as the inverse image of the diagonal under squared determinant characters, then dévissage SG* → μ2×μ2 with kernel an extension of G_m by norm-one tori ST_ρ × ST_σ
ideas.modern_name: Dévissage of a diagonalisable / multiplicative-type group scheme into tori and finite parts
ideas.where_published: general theory in SGA3; this specific computation unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: A routine structural computation of a small group scheme, by monomorphism, image equations and exact sequences, inside a larger unpublished project. There is no new idea or connection on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: The group in the projection is SG**_{ρ,σ}(0) (superscript '**', argument '(0)'), not 'SG*_{ρ,σ}(ω)'. The same applies to the later homomorphism to μ2×μ2.
Line 'est mono, et induit un iso. de SG**_{ρ,σ}(0) sur le sous-groupe de T_ρ × N'_σ défini par les équations' — the '(0)' is clearly visible in the image.
The insertion under 'diagonale' reads 'de G_m × G_m' and is placed above 'par'.
